parents of children with CF or intermediate CF classification perceive their child to be vulnerable and less protected compared to parents of healthy children.

parents of children with intermediate CF classification perceive their children as more vulnerable than parents of healthy children and parents of children with cystic fibrosis but perceive their children to be less vulnerable than children with cystic fibers.

parents of children with CF and I-group parents perceive their children to be at greater risk of developing CF symptoms than H-group parents, but I-group parents have lower expectations of their children developing CF symptoms than parents in the other two groups.

the impact of intermediate classification on parents' perceptions of child vulnerability, which in turn, influences their perceptions of child protectiveness.

the ICF classification is a useful tool to assess parental perceptions and that the I-group may be a useful group to study for future interventions to reduce parental anxiety.

parents of children with CF or intermediate classification perceive their children as more vulnerable to illness than healthy children, and that parents of children in the intermediate classification perceive their child as less vulnerable than parents of children with cystic fibrosis.
